findings.description: The RDS instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, so all data and automated snapshots are stored unencrypted. Anyone who obtains the underlying storage or a snapshot can read the catalog database contents in plaintext.

The instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving the MySQL endpoint a public IP so that anyone on the internet can attempt to reach the database; combined with the default admin username this greatly expands the brute-force and direct-exploitation attack surface.

The master username is the fixed default 'admin'. Predictable administrative account names are trivially targeted by credential-stuffing and brute-force attacks and violate the guidance against default administrative account names surviving into deployed infrastructure.

The database master password is interpolated into the EC2 user_data startup script (DB_PASSWORD), and the same var.password is used as the DB master password. User data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, and the plaintext secret is also stored in Terraform state, so the credential is exposed well beyond the secret store.

The master password is supplied as a literal Terraform variable value on the aws_db_instance, which persists it in plaintext in state files; the lifecycle ignore_changes block only masks drift and does not reduce this exposure.

The user_data script embeds DB_SERVER, DB_USERNAME and especially DB_PASSWORD into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc as PHP defines. Anyone with describe/instance-metadata access, or any file-read on the host, can recover the database credentials in plaintext.

findings.issue_category: unrestricted ingress via attached security group
findings.description: The instance attaches aws_security_group.portal_sg and exposes an Apache web server on a public DNS name; the application is intentionally internet-facing, so any ingress rules on that group that admit 0.0.0.0/0 directly expose the workload.

The EC2 instance does not set metadata_options http_tokens = "required", leaving the legacy IMDSv1 endpoint enabled. The hosted PHP application accepts user input and performs HTTP requests, so an SSRF can retrieve the instance-profile credentials without authentication.

The database security group allows all protocols and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This provides an unrestricted exfiltration path for database contents and a channel for command-and-control traffic from a compromised database host.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", which is effectively administrative access over storage, compute and database services. A compromise of the catalog application instance immediately yields full control of these services across the account.

The role has broad permissions and no permissions boundary is attached, so any principal able to modify the role can escalate to full s3/ec2/rds control without a guardrail limiting maximum delegation.

monitoring_interval = 0 disables Enhanced Monitoring and the instance has no dedicated audit/security logging configuration, so database-level security-relevant activity is not recorded. (Reported only as it relates to audit-trail coverage; retentin/sizing concerns are excluded.)

The startup script writes dbinfo.inc containing the DB password beneath /var/www and includes it from index.php; if the web server ever serves the include directory or a PHP handler fails, the credential file becomes remotely readable.
